reading.body:
Flexential Minneapolis - Chaska publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 160,838 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same power supports roughly 900 racks. The operator publishes no breakdown of how that space or power is allocated, so which density applies is not known from this data.

The certifications qualify the campus to host a specific set of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls auditing. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued. No tenant names are published.

Among the 13 Minnesota facilities this site has mapped, Chaska is the only one whose operator has published a megawatt figure, and that figure is 9 MW, making it rank first by published IT capacity in the state. That ranking reflects the limits of available data, not a confirmed physical supremacy: twelve other mapped facilities publish no capacity number at all, so their true scale is unknown from operator spec pages this site has read.
